newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish, Swedish beet planting seen in April.
newsitem.headline: Danish, Swedish beet planting seen in April.

text.p: Danish packaging, food and sugar producer Danisco said on Friday it expected to begin sugar beet sowing in Denmark and Sweden in April, depending very much on weather conditions.
"We normally start our sowing campaigns in April but it is too early to say much at this stage. The actual start depends completely on the weather," a Danisco spokesman told Reuters.

He said Denmark's most intense sugar plantings took place in the southern islands of Lolland and Falster and in south Zealand, with more scattered cultivation in the rest of Zealand and Funen and east Jutland to the west.
Most Swedish planting took place in the south.
The spokesman said it would be impossible to give a realistic idea of sowing campaign progress until April.
Danisco, Europe's fourth biggest sugar producer, has a virtual monopoly of sugar production in Denmark and Sweden, with areas also in eastern Germany.
